name: frappe-assets
description: Desk frontend framework for Frappe apps — a design system, a spec renderer and a dashboard module
//sideEffects: The toolkit is pure — every module earns its place by being imported for an export, so a consuming bundler may drop whatever a dashboard does not use. This became true rather than merely claimed in v0.3.0: `charts.js` used to construct a MutationObserver at module scope, which meant importing anything at all touched `document.documentElement`. It is now installed on the first chart mounted. Two exceptions must stay listed. `demo/`: `gallery.js` pulls in `frappe-stub.js` as a bare import for its side effects alone, and under a blanket `false` esbuild removes that import and the gallery dies on the first `t()`. `charts/echarts.js`: importing it IS the interface — it registers the engine — so a bundler entitled to drop a bare import would take the registration with it and every chart panel would then throw. `dashboard/panels/index.js`: same shape, and esbuild said so out loud — `Ignoring this import because "dashboard/panels/index.js" was marked as having no side effects`, which would have shipped a renderer that knows no panel types at all.
//exports: Named entries and no wildcard, on purpose. `CONTRACT.md` promises the barrel, the dashboard module, the chart engine entry and the stylesheet; a deep import of any other file is not supported, and a `./*` wildcard would turn every internal module into an accidental contract that nothing then dares rename. `./charts/echarts` is its own entry because that is what keeps ~550 KB of charting engine out of an app that draws no charts. The SCSS is reachable by path because an app's stylesheet imports it as `~frappe-assets/ui/styles/dash.scss` through sass includePaths, which does not consult this field — the entry is here so a bundler that does consult it agrees.
//files: Every module directory the barrel can reach, and nothing else. `demo/` and `test/` are development tools; yarn clones the whole git repo regardless of this field, so leaving them out is documentation of intent rather than a size saving — but a consumer importing from either is doing something the contract does not cover.
//devDependencies: Gallery build and test suite only. Yarn does not install a git dependency's devDependencies, so none of this reaches a consuming app. The script is named `demo` and not `prepare` for the same reason: yarn runs `prepare` for git deps, and every app installing this would start building the gallery.
